context.guidance: Erase Personal Data once its Purpose is served, by wiring erasure into account-closure and end-of-purpose events rather than leaving the records in place. §8(7)(a) is the erasure duty this Issue Type cites for that case. Where Rule 8(1) applies to a Third Schedule class, schedule the erasure job from the retention period the Third Schedule sets.

value.fix: With `paranoid: true`, Sequelize does a soft delete. `destroy()` only fills in `deletedAt` and leaves the personal data in the table, so closing an account doesn't erase anything as §8(7)(a) requires. To fix it: (1) For tables that hold personal data, set `paranoid: false`, or keep soft delete only as a short undo window. (2) In the account-closure and end-of-purpose handlers, call `Model.destroy({ where: { userId }, force: true })` on this model and on every associated model that holds personal data, all inside one transaction. Use `onDelete: 'CASCADE'` on the associations or delete the children explicitly. Where a record has to stay for legal or audit reasons, overwrite its personal fields with null or a non-reversible token instead of keeping the real values. (3) Add a scheduled purge job, such as a daily cron, that runs `Model.destroy({ where: { deletedAt: { [Op.lt]: cutoff } }, force: true, paranoid: false })`. Set the cutoff from the documented purpose-retention period. If Rule 8(1) applies to a Third Schedule class, use the retention period the Third Schedule sets for that class, and erase once it ends after the user's last interaction. Send the 48-hour pre-erasure notice that Rule 8(2) requires. (4) Remove the data from backups, caches, search indexes and processors too, log each erasure without storing the erased personal data, and add a test that checks the rows are physically gone after closure and after the purge runs.
